title: ProviderCredentialUpdate
description: Body of PATCH /provider-credentials/{credentialId}. Absent = unchanged; none of these fields is nullable; an empty body changes nothing. Permission: providers.update; a `key` that rotates the credential also needs providers.create. `provider` is create-only — echoed back it must be the current provider (else 422 immutable_field). Unknown keys are a 422.

enabled.description: Absent = true on create, unchanged on update or replace. Boolean only: null is a 422.

key.description: Write-only. Sending the key already stored is a no-op (no verification, no audit entry, no config re-projection), so a client may send its configured key on every update — as Terraform does. A different key rotates the credential in place: it is verified against the provider, resealed and given a new fingerprint on the same id, and the gateway switches to it without a gap. A rejected key is a 422 validation_failed on `key` and leaves the stored key unchanged. Compare fingerprint to detect a key changed outside your configuration.

id.description: Response field (read-only). Absent or null on create; on update it may be echoed back only with its current value — anything else is a 422 immutable_field.

provider.description: Create-only: on update it may be echoed back only with its current value — anything else is a 422 immutable_field. Changing it means replacing the resource.

fingerprint.description: Response field (read-only). Absent or null on create; on update it may be echoed back only with its current value — anything else is a 422 immutable_field.

created_at.description: Response field (read-only). Absent or null on create; on update it may be echoed back only with its current value — anything else is a 422 immutable_field.

updated_at.description: Response field (read-only). Absent or null on create; on update it may be echoed back only with its current value — anything else is a 422 immutable_field.
